front_blocks.md: How does the behaviour of the **cell surface membrane** during division differ between animal and plant cells?

back_blocks.md: In **animal cells**, the cell surface membrane **pinches inwards** to divide the cell.
In **plant cells**, a **new cell wall (cell plate)** forms across the middle instead.

front_blocks.md: Why are **root tips** used to observe mitosis?

back_blocks.md: The tip of a root contains a region of **actively dividing cells**, so many cells are caught in the process of **mitosis**.

front_blocks.md: How can you identify which **stage of mitosis** a cell is in?

back_blocks.md: By the **position and appearance of the chromosomes**, e.g. chromosomes lined up along the equator indicate **metaphase**.

cards.front_md: How can you identify which **stage of mitosis** a cell is in?

front_blocks.md: In a photomicrograph, how would you identify a cell in **anaphase**?

back_blocks.md: The **chromatids are separating** and being pulled towards **opposite poles** of the cell.

front_blocks.md: Outline how to prepare a **root tip squash** to observe mitosis.

back_blocks.md: **Cut** the tip from a growing root.
**Stain** it so the chromosomes become visible.
**Squash** the tip on a slide to spread the cells into a single layer.
View under a **microscope**.

front_blocks.md: Most cells in a root tip sample are in mitosis at any one time.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Most cells are in **interphase**; only a small proportion are actively undergoing mitosis at any one time.
